claim: Entity-vs-entity collision is a box broad-phase: HITEM tests the X intersection of the two collision boxes first, then the Y intersection, before any pixel-span work.
Broad-phase X test: HITEM compares the two objects' X positions against their collision boxes (WITHIN X INTERSECTION SQUARES?).

source.verbatim: LDD	PPOSX,U		WITHIN X INTERSECTION SQUARES?

claim: Broad-phase Y test: after X passes, HITEM checks the Y box intersection (WITHIN Y INTERSECTION SQUARES?) using PCOLY1/PCOLY2 — bottom/top of the rough box.

source.verbatim: LDD	PCOLY1,X	WITHIN Y INTERSECTION SQUARES?

claim: Narrow phase indirect-loads the frame record's collision-span pointer (the per-scanline mask) via the picture handle PPICH.
The narrow-phase pixel-span walker is BPCOL: it steps the two collision-span tables scanline-aligned looking for an overlapping (left,right) pair.
PPOSY is a THREE-byte field [super-high, whole PIXEL, fraction], big-endian. The whole-pixel word is at offset +0..+1; the 8.8 pixel:fraction word the flight core integrates is at PPOSY+1..+2.

source.verbatim: PPOSY	RMB	3	PROCESS'S OBJECT Y LOCATION (AND FRACTIONAL DISTANCE)

claim: THE JOUST is decided on WHOLE PIXELS, fraction EXCLUDED: OSTBO reads PPOSY at offset +0 (the [super-high, pixel] word) via ADDD PPOSY,X — NOT PPOSY+1 (the 8.8 word). This corrects the dossier prose 'fraction included' (subsystems.md:137-139), a jt1-10-class wrong-prose citation.

source.verbatim: ADDD	PPOSY,X		 (DETERMINATION OF WHO IS KILLED)

claim: OSTBO forms (PLANTZ,X + PPOSY,X) − (PLANTZ,U + PPOSY,U) on the whole-pixel word (SUBD PPOSY,U, again offset +0, no +1).
Exact tie in the whole-pixel joust height = BOTH bounce: BEQ branches to the 'PLAYERS COLIDE' bounce path when the difference is zero (BR=BOTH ON SAME LEVEL).
Otherwise the strictly-smaller (higher on screen) height wins: BMI (difference negative → REG.X higher) takes the victor path OSTXT3; a positive difference falls through to OSTPYP.
The tie path is a pure bounce (no kill): it plays the 'players collide' clank and branches to the bounce restore, skipping OSTWIN — nobody is killed on an exact-height tie.
The 8.8 (pixel.fraction) Y value the FLIGHT core integrates lives at PPOSY+1 ('ADD IN FRACTIONAL DISTANCE') — the +1 that OSTBO deliberately omits, proving OSTBO's offset-0 read is the whole pixel.

source.verbatim: ADDGRX	ADDD	PPOSY+1,U	ADD IN FRACTIONAL DISTANCE

claim: PLANTZ = 2 while skidding is TWO WHOLE PIXELS lower ('SKIDDING OSTRICH HAS A LANTZ 2 PIXELS LOWER') — only consistent with the whole-pixel joust compare; a fractional add of 2 would be 2/256 px, not the documented 2 pixels.

source.verbatim: LDB	#2		SKIDDING OSTRICH HAS A LANTZ 2 PIXELS LOWER

claim: Skidding stores the lance offset to PLANTZ (STB PLANTZ,U) — the register OSTBO adds to the whole-pixel Y.

PFACE is the facing register: 0 = right-faced, non-zero = left-faced. The ground state machine's onPlus/onMinus transitions are FACING-relative (joystick vs PFACE); adding facing makes the onMinus reversal/skid chain reachable (the jt1-6 gap).
Enemies never kill each other: OSTHIT ANDs the two PIDs and, on the enemy-vs-enemy class bit, branches to the no-kill bounce path.

source.verbatim: LDA	PID,U		ENEMIES DO NOT KILL EACH OTHER

claim: The enemy-vs-enemy (and ptero-vs-ptero) contact branches to OSTHT2 = NO KILL, a bump-only bounce.

source.verbatim: BNE	OSTHT2		 BR=NO KILL (ENEMY VS. ENEMY, PTERO VS. PTERO)

claim: Bounce-apart vertical (winner/top): OSTXUP loads −2 into PBUMPY,X — the one on top is shoved UP by two pixels.
OSTXUP stores the −2 to PBUMPY of the top object (X IS ON TOP, MAKE X GO UP); a downward 'wrong-way' velocity is then inverted and halved (COMA/NEGB/SBCA/ASRA/RORB).

source.verbatim: STA	PBUMPY,X		X IS ON TOP, MAKE X GO UP

claim: Bounce-apart vertical (loser/bottom): OSTXDN loads +2 into PBUMPY,X — the one on the bottom is shoved DOWN by two pixels.
OSTXDN stores the +2 to PBUMPY of the bottom object (U IS ON TOP, MAKE X LOWER); an upward 'wrong-way' velocity is inverted and halved.

source.verbatim: STA	PBUMPY,X		U IS ON TOP, MAKE X LOWER

claim: Bounce-apart horizontal: on a same-level (COLDX≠0) hit, OSTXLF reverses the entity's own X velocity (NEGA) and slows it by 2.

source.verbatim: OSTXLF	LDA	PVELX,X		U IS ON RIGHT, MOVE X LEFT

claim: The +2 is the 'slow down a bit' term applied to the reversed X velocity before half of it is handed to the other object as PBUMPX.
The horizontal shove passed to the OTHER object is HALVED (ASRA, a signed shift-right) before being stored.
The halved reversed velocity is stored as the other object's PBUMPX one-shot horizontal shove.
PBUMPX is a one-shot horizontal shove drained at most 3 px/frame: WRAPX loads the register (ALSO ADD IN BUMP REGISTER) before applying at most ±3 to this frame's delta.

source.verbatim: WRAPX	LDA	PBUMPX,U	ALSO ADD IN BUMP REGISTER

claim: PBUMPX drain: while the register exceeds 3 (CMPA #3), spend 3 this frame and keep the rest for next frame.
PBUMPX drain: the register is reduced by 3 each frame it is over the cap (SUBA #3, stored back to PBUMPX).
PBUMPX drain: once the remaining shove is within ±3 (WRPBRM) it is applied whole and the register cleared.

source.verbatim: CLR	PBUMPX,U		AND RESET BUMP REGISTER

claim: PBUMPY is consumed WHOLE in a single frame: it is added directly to the whole-pixel Y (ADDA PBUMPY,U, A being the pixel byte after the 8.8 integration).

source.verbatim: ADDA	PBUMPY,U	ADD IN BUMPING REGISTER

claim: PBUMPY is cleared the same frame it is applied (CLR PBUMPY,U) — a one-shot vertical shove, unlike the multi-frame PBUMPX drain.
DVALUE is the per-decision-block byte holding the kill score, encoded in thousands/hundreds nibbles — decoded by the block's DVALUR routine (SCRTEN or SCRHUN), not a plain ×100.

source.verbatim: DVALUE	RMB	1	SCORE WHEN KILLED (IN THOUSANDS/HUNDREDS)

claim: On a kill, OSTWIN fetches the dead object's decision block and reads its DVALUE byte (GET DEAD OBJECTS SCORE) — the score EVENT value; accumulation is jt4.

source.verbatim: LDY	PDECSN,U	GET DEAD OBJECTS SCORE

claim: OSTWIN loads the dead object's DVALUE score byte into A.
OSTWIN dispatches the block's DVALUR score routine (SCRTEN for bounder/hunter, SCRHUN for the shadow lord), which turns the DVALUE byte into the awarded points.
The bounder decision block P4DEC promotes LINET → BOUNDR and scores via SCRTEN.
Bounder DVALUE = $05: via SCRTEN (tens high-nibble, hundreds low-nibble) = 0 tens + 5 hundreds = 500 points.
The hunter decision block P5DEC promotes LINET → B2UNDR and scores via SCRTEN.

Hunter DVALUE = $57: via SCRTEN (tens high-nibble, hundreds low-nibble) = 5 tens + 7 hundreds = 750 points. A naïve ×100 of $57 would give 5700 — the trap SCRTEN's backwards tens/hundreds decode avoids.
The shadow-lord decision block P6DEC promotes LINET → SHADOW and scores via SCRHUN.
Shadow-lord DVALUE = $15: via SCRHUN (thousands high-nibble, hundreds low-nibble) = 1 thousand + 5 hundreds = 1500 points.
SCRTEN (bounder/hunter DVALUR): decodes the DVALUE byte as tens (high nibble) and hundreds (low nibble) — the 'HUNDREDS AND TENS (BACKWARDS)' routine.

source.verbatim: SCRTEN	LDY	DSCORE,X	GET SCORE AREA

claim: SCRTEN masks the high nibble as the TENS digit (ANDA #$F0, 'SCORE TENS').
SCRTEN masks the low nibble as the HUNDREDS digit (ANDB #$0F, '& HUNDREDS') — so $57 = 5 tens + 7 hundreds = 750.
SCRHUN (shadow-lord DVALUR): decodes the DVALUE byte as thousands (high nibble) and hundreds (low nibble) directly — 'INCREMENT SCORE BY THOUSANDS AND HUNDREDS' — so $15 = 1500.

source.verbatim: SCRHUN	LDY	DSCORE,X	GET SCORE AREA

claim: PBUMPX is the horizontal bump register (BUMPING DELTA X) — the one-shot shove drained by WRAPX.
PBUMPY is the vertical bump register (BUMP REGISTER IN Y DIRECTION) — consumed whole each frame.

source.verbatim: PBUMPY	RMB	1		BUMP REGISTER IN Y DIRECTION

claim: PLANTZ is the lance-height offset for skidding — added to the whole-pixel Y in the joust determination.

source.verbatim: PLANTZ	RMB	1		LANTZ OFFSET FOR SKIDDING

claim: The collision box's Y bounds are PCOLY1 (bottom line of the rough box) and PCOLY2 (top) — the HITEM broad-phase Y intersection operands.

source.verbatim: PCOLY1	RMB	1		COLISION DETECTS BOTTOM LINE OF ROUGH BOX

claim: PCOLX is the collision box's right-hand X bound — the HITEM broad-phase X intersection operand.

source.verbatim: PCOLX	RMB	2		COLISION DETECT RIGHT HAND SIDE OF COLISION
